title: Working Memory Model: Evaluation
welcome_lead: Strengths, criticisms and the central executive problem.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology WMM evaluation: strengths, central executive limitations, comparison to MSM.
final_note: A model is only as good as what it cannot yet explain.

walkthroughs.body_html: The WMM explains data the MSM cannot — dual-task interference patterns, KF case. It's been applied to education (dyslexia involves phonological loop deficits, Hatcher 2002), to reading comprehension and to mental arithmetic. Its modular structure is supported by brain imaging.

The central executive is the model's weakest link — vague, possibly itself multi-component. Eslinger & Damasio (1985) studied patient EVR with damaged frontal lobe: good problem-solving but poor decision-making — central executive may be multiple subsystems.

The MSM is simpler and better for explaining flow into LTM but cannot account for STM as workspace. The WMM is detailed about STM but says little about LTM. Cowan (2005) proposed an embedded process model that integrates both.
